correctness.rationale: For ordered normalized horizontal coordinates, integrating the vertical difference between each quadratic secant and the parabola gives area/H=s^3-sum(gap^3), H=a*l^3/6. The n-2 interior order statistics conditioned on extremes produce m=n-1 Dirichlet(1,...,1) spacings; the free sample range has Beta(n-1,2) independent of internal normalized gaps. Direct Dirichlet rising-factorial calculations give E[Z]=6/[n(n+1)], E[Z^2]=36(n+18)/[n(n+1)(n+2)(n+3)(n+4)] and the stated variances; beta third/sixth moments give the full free variance polynomial. The two extreme deficits n*T_(1) and n*(1-T_(n)) converge jointly to iid exponential(1), hence n(1-S^3)->3 Gamma(2,1). Exponential Dirichlet representation gives a bivariate CLT for (mean E, mean E^3), delta-method gradient (-18,1), variance 324+684-648=360; exact range/shape independence yields the joint independent Gaussian correction. All n>=3, arbitrary affine graph terms and a>0 survive normalization; finite tests are not limit proofs.

value.rationale: Fixing versus not fixing endpoints is a canonical sampling-design choice for convex-boundary approximation. The exact beta-Dirichlet coupling separates endpoint uncertainty from interior spacing noise and explains the non-Gaussian order-n^-1 missing-area law versus order-n^-5/2 centered Gaussian fluctuations; complete finite-size moments quantitatively support that structural difference.

limitations: Uniform horizontal, not arc-length, on one strictly convex quadratic graph; n>=3; no general smooth-curve Gamma law, no elementary finite-n density or certification of all historical literature.
